blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Game engines and coding agents can specify the layout, motion, and camera of a scene, yet turning such coarse structure into realistic video requires a renderer that follows the structure and completes the appearance it leaves open. Existing renderers are tied to the representation of one engine, need tens of denoising steps or a costly distillation of their own, and learn from conditions that are not aligned with their target videos. We present SolarRenderer, a structure-conditioned video renderer that adapts a frozen MiniMax-H3 33B backbone with two lightweight LoRAs. Structural videos enter the native reference pathway of the backbone at the positions of the frames they describe, without a type identifier and described only in plain text, so that a single control LoRA follows arbitrary structural representations. Starting from a pretrained four-step LoRA, structure-guided distribution matching renders in four steps, 12.3 times faster than 50-step sampling, while preserving the learned control. A block-causal variant extends the same design to streaming and renders 768p video in real time. To train the model, we build a frame-aligned corpus of 136K clips from game engines, simulators, and YouTube videos. Experiments on an in-distribution test set and a generalization benchmark of 16 structural representations show that SolarRenderer achieves state-of-the-art results across both, and generalizes to 11 unseen representations, including pose skeletons, drawings, and point clouds.
blocks.zh: 游戏引擎和编码代理可以指定一个场景的布局,运动,和相机,然而将这种粗糙的结构变成现实的视频需要一个遵循结构的渲染器,完成它留下的外观打开. 现有的渲染器与一种发动机的表示有关,需要数十个调试步骤或自己的昂贵的蒸馏,并学习与其目标视频不匹配的条件. 我们介绍SolarRenderer,一个结构条件化的视频渲染器,它可以改造一个冷冻的MiniMax-H3 33B主干线,有两个轻量级的LORA. 结构视频在其描述的框架位置输入主干线的原生参考路径,没有类型标识符,仅在纯文本中描述,因此一个单一的控制LORA遵循任意的结构表示. 从预先训练的四步LORA开始,结构制导的分布比对在四个步骤中,比50步的取样速度快12.3倍,同时保留了学到的控制. 区块-causal变体将同一设计延伸至流线,实时制作768p视频. 为了训练这个模型,我们从游戏引擎、模拟器和YouTube视频中构建了一套由136K片段组成的帧组合。 对分布式测试集的实验和16个结构表示式的概括化基准表明,SolarRenderer在两个方面都取得了最先进的结果,并概括到11个看不见的表示式,包括姿势骨架,图画,和点云.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Video generation models now produce realistic footage from a text prompt
or a single image. However, visual realism alone does not ensure consistent
3D geometry, physically plausible dynamics, or temporal
coherence [ Huang et al., 2024 ; Bansal et al., 2025 ; Lu et al., 2026a ; Ying et al., 2026 ; Lu et al., 2026c ] . In game development, film previsualization, and
agent-driven content creation, creators often specify the scene
layout, object motion, and camera trajectory in advance. Designers block out scenes, animators key character motion, and coding
agents script camera paths. These structural priors turn the task into
rendering: producing realistic video that follows the specified scene and
its evolution. With geometry and dynamics specified by these priors, the
video model can focus on appearance synthesis, reducing the scope for
structural and temporal drift. Recent systems therefore link executable world state to
video generation through proxy videos [ Chen et al., 2026b ] or engine
buffers [ Zhan et al., 2026 ; Lin et al., 2026a ] , so that the engine determines scene evolution and a video model renders it .

Building such a renderer still faces three problems. First, control is tied to a fixed set of representations . Engine-driven
renderers are built around the one representation their engine exports,
such as white-box frames [ Zhan et al., 2026 ] , semantic maps [ Lu et al., 2026d ] , proxy videos [ Chen et al., 2026b ] , or full
G-buffers [ Lin et al., 2026a ] , and general controllable generators
attach a branch per condition [ Zhang et al., 2023 ; NVIDIA, 2025 ] or label the type of each input [ Mao et al., 2026 ] ,
so a new engine or a new kind of proxy calls for a new model. Second,
rendering is slow . A large video backbone needs tens of
denoising steps, and distilling a structure-conditioned
model of this size from scratch is costly [ Lin et al., 2026a ] , which
keeps such renderers far from interactive use. Third, training pairs are rarely aligned frame by frame . Conditions estimated from
real videos carry estimator errors and differ from engine proxies [ Xu et al., 2026 ] , and engine-paired data so far come from a single
engine.

We evaluate \texorpdfstring \pdfxform D SolarRenderer on an in-distribution test set with ground-truth
videos and on a generalization benchmark that covers 16 structural
representations, 11 of them unseen in training. The results show that our four-step model outperforms existing acceleration LoRAs and the official
backbone, surpasses existing structure-conditioned renderers, and achieves
a new state of the art in structure-conditioned video
rendering. Notably, our method shows strong generalization to
unseen structure . It faithfully renders pose skeletons, pencil
storyboards, children’s crayon drawings, wireframes, and point clouds,
none of which appears in training. Our contributions are fourfold: [itemsep=3pt] • We present a renderer that handles any structural
representation with a single control LoRA through the native reference
pathway, without type identifiers or added branches. • We propose structure-guided distribution matching , which
post-trains a pretrained four-step LoRA so that our model renders in four steps while preserving its structural control. • We build a frame-aligned paired corpus of 136K clips from
game engines, simulators, and YouTube videos, in which every structural
frame is aligned with its target frame. • Our method achieves state-of-the-art results on an
in-distribution test set and a generalization benchmark of 16 structural
representations, including 11 unseen in training, and its causal variant
renders 768p video in real time .

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Rendering Engine and Agent State into Video. World modeling encompasses 3D and 4D scene generation [ Kong et al., 2025 ] and interactive proxies that provide feedback for agent
learning [ Yang et al., 2026b ] .
Recent systems let a game engine, a simulator, or a coding agent decide what
happens in a scene and let a video model render it. Most of them train a
renderer on one structural representation exported by their engine, such as
white-box frames [ Zhan et al., 2026 ; Gomez-Nogales et al., 2026 ] , semantic
maps [ Lu et al., 2026d ] , depth and normal
maps [ Chi et al., 2026 ] , projected 3D
boxes [ Huang et al., 2026b ] , or the proxy video of a code world
model [ Chen et al., 2026b ; Liao and Liu, 2026 ] , and several distill the
renderer to a few streaming steps for real-time
use [ VAST-AI-Research, 2026 ; Lu et al., 2026d ] . A
related branch renders from full G-buffers that also carry materials and
lighting [ Zeng et al., 2026 ; Lin et al., 2026a ; Huang et al., 2026c ; Liang et al., 2025 ] .
Other works avoid paired proxy data, either by learning from posed RGB-D
video [ Xu et al., 2026 ] or by showing proxy renders to a frozen model
during the early denoising steps only [ Liang et al., 2026 ] .
However, each renderer is built around the representation of its own
engine, so a new engine or a new kind of proxy calls for a new renderer. \texorpdfstring \pdfxform D SolarRenderer follows many kinds of structure with a single
control LoRA ,
including structure it has never seen.

blocks.en:
Structure-Conditioned Video Generation. Controllable video generation commonly injects conditions in one of two
ways. Branch-based methods attach a trainable copy or added control blocks
to the backbone, from ControlNet [ Zhang et al., 2023 ] to
multi-condition variants on video
backbones [ Alibaba PAI, 2026 ; NVIDIA, 2025 ; NVIDIA et al., 2025 ; Jiang et al., 2025 ] .
Sequence-based methods place condition tokens next to the target tokens and
read them with full attention, often through a small
LoRA [ Tan et al., 2025 ; Ju et al., 2025 ; Fang et al., 2025 ; Mao et al., 2026 ; Tang et al., 2026 ; Gao et al., 2026 ] .
Further works steer generation through warped noise, 3D tracking videos,
reference videos, predicted LoRAs, or jointly generated intrinsic
channels [ Burgert et al., 2025 ; Gu et al., 2025 ; Bian et al., 2026 ; Wu et al., 2026 ; Xi et al., 2025 ; Lu et al., 2026b ] ,
and training-free methods condition an existing model through structured
first frames or a ControlNet-style world
model [ Li et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025b ] . However, these methods
add parameters for control, label the type of each condition, or are
trained on a fixed set of condition kinds. \texorpdfstring \pdfxform D SolarRenderer passes an untyped structural
video through the native reference pathway of the backbone with one LoRA,
so that the same model also follows structure unseen in training.

Few-Step Distillation and Acceleration Adapters. Few-step video generation is usually obtained in two ways. One distills a
multi-step teacher into a few-step student by distribution
matching [ Yin et al., 2024b ; Yin et al., 2024a ; Liu et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026c ; Yu et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2025 ; Zhao et al., 2026 ] or consistency and flow-map distillation [ Zheng et al., 2026 ; Gu et al., 2026 ] . The other
trains a plug-in acceleration LoRA once on a base model and attaches it to
models derived from the same
base [ Luo et al., 2023 ; Lin and Yang, 2024 ; Yang et al., 2026a ; Hao AI Lab, 2026 ] ,
with recent work making such LoRAs transferable between base and distilled
models [ Li et al., 2026b ; Wang et al., 2026b ] . For conditional models, several
works distill the conditional model itself or re-tune its control module
after distillation [ Wang et al., 2026a ; Li et al., 2026a ; Sun et al., 2026 ] ,
and MotionEcho [ Rong et al., 2025 ] restores motion control at
inference with guidance from the slow teacher. However, distilling a large
control model from scratch is costly, and a generic few-step adapter attached
unchanged lowers the visual quality and first-frame fidelity of the control
model. \texorpdfstring \pdfxform D SolarRenderer post-trains a four-step LoRA on
the frozen control model, with a distribution-matching teacher extrapolated
toward its structure-conditioned prediction.

Native Reference Pathway. A renderer must match every structural frame with the target frame it
describes. Instead of attaching a ControlNet branch [ Zhang et al., 2023 ] or concatenating channels, both of which
introduce parameters trained from scratch, we feed the structural video
and the optional first frame through the reference pathway of the
backbone [ MiniMax, 2026 ] . This pathway packs text, reference videos,
audio, and the target video into one full-attention sequence
( \cref fig:pipeline), so the control adapter can inherit the pretrained ability to read reference
videos . We refer to the tokens of the supplied references as reference tokens and to those of the generated video as target tokens . Yet native reference tokens occupy a separate
temporal segment before the clip and their own spatial grid, so the
zero-shot backbone uses a structural video as a loose reference and
copies it or changes the camera instead of following
the structure.

depend on the relative offset between tokens, we supply the missing

control learned at full steps. Training both objectives together does not
achieve this, because whenever the acceleration objective can update the

a few-step student from scratch is costly at this scale and prone to
instability [ Lin et al., 2026a ] . We therefore decouple control and acceleration into two stages on
one frozen backbone, which also preserves its visual prior and keeps it
compatible with adapters trained on the same weights.

blocks.en: 3.4 Causal Streaming Extension
blocks.zh: 3.4 因果流线扩展

blocks.en:
To generate video incrementally, we extend the same two-stage design to
block-causal attention. The clip is split into blocks of at most five
latent frames. We adapt the bidirectional control LoRA with teacher forcing
so that each block attends to the prompt, the first frame, the structure of
itself and the five preceding blocks, and the clean frames of the five
preceding blocks, never to a later block. We then freeze this causal
control LoRA and post-train a separate acceleration LoRA, initialized from
the bidirectional four-step LoRA, on the student’s own block-by-block
rollouts, with the bidirectional control model as the structure-guided
teacher ( w = 1.5 w=1.5 ). Each rollout is generated without gradients and replayed
as one teacher-forced sequence, so that the gradient reaches both how each
block is generated and how it serves as context for later blocks. At
inference, we merge the acceleration LoRA into the backbone, keep the control LoRA
attached, sample each block in four steps, and update the fixed-window key–value cache before outputting the
block immediately. With a streaming VAE decoder [ Chen et al., 2026a ] that
decodes each block without future latents, the causal model renders 768p
video in real time at up to 28 FPS.

A renderer learns to follow structure only from pairs in which the target
video actually follows the structure. Conditions estimated from real
videos, such as predicted depth or segmentation, carry the errors of the
estimator and differ from the engine proxies that the renderer receives at
test time. We therefore collect pairs whose condition is exported by an
engine or fitted to the target, and use a pair as structural supervision
only when its condition matches the target in time and carries enough
structure. We then describe the data sources ( \cref sec:sources), the
checks that decide how each source is used ( \cref sec:alignment), and the
construction of prompts ( \cref sec:captions).

blocks.en: 4.2 Data Checks
blocks.zh: 4.2 (中文(简体) ). 数据检查

blocks.en:
A condition can fail in two ways. It can be offset from the target in time
or space, or it can be aligned yet too coarse to describe the target. We
therefore run two checks on every source.
blocks.zh:
一个条件可以从两个方面失效. 可以及时从目标中抵消
或空间,或者它可能过于粗糙,无法描述目标。 我们
因此,对每个来源进行两次检查。

blocks.en:
Temporal and Spatial Agreement. For timing, we correlate the motion of each condition with that of its
target over a range of frame offsets. The offset at which the correlation
peaks shows whether the two are synchronized, and clips whose peak is not
at zero offset are removed. For space, we measure the recall of the
condition edges in the target frame and compare it with the recall of the
horizontally mirrored condition. A condition that matches its target
recovers clearly more edges than its mirror, so clips without this margin
are removed as spatially misaligned. Further filters remove near-duplicates,
dark or low-contrast clips, and clips whose condition covers too little of
the frame. Finally, we manually inspect samples from every source before
it enters training.

Evaluation Protocol. We assess every method with pairwise judgments and automatic scores. • Pairwise judgment is our primary measure. Gemini 3.8 Flash [ Google DeepMind, 2026 ; Gemini Team, 2023 ] receives the structural video, the first frame, and two renderings, and
compares them on 1 visual quality , 2 adherence to the structure and motion , 3 preservation of the first frame , and 4 overall preference . Each pair is judged in
both orders. We report the net score of ours against each
compared method as (wins − - losses)/cases, the difference between our
win and loss rates. It ranges from − 1 -1 to 1 1 , with positive values
indicating a preference for ours. From the verdicts between all pairs of methods on a test
set we fit one Bradley–Terry model [ Bradley and Terry, 1952 ] per judge
question and report the strength of every method as an Elo
rating , with the mean of the compared methods at 1000. A blind human study agrees
with the verdicts of the judge. • Automatic metrics , grouped into 1 quality (DOVER [ Wu et al., 2023 ] , LAION
aesthetics [ Schuhmann, 2022 ] , VideoScore2 [ He et al., 2025 ] ), 2 stability (flow-warping residual and adjacent-frame DINOv2 similarity [ Oquab et al., 2023 ] ), 3 control (CoTracker3
track error [ Karaev et al., 2025 ] and edge F1 against the
structure), and 4 first-frame preservation (DINOv2 similarity of the last second to the first frame). Each metric
is mapped linearly from a fixed range to 0–100, and the automatic score averages the metrics within each group and then
the four groups. Details of the protocol and the full results are given in \cref app:evaluation,app:results.

Comparison with Structure-Conditioned Renderers. \texorpdfstring \pdfxform D SolarRenderer reaches the best rating on every judge question of
both test sets ( \cref tab:main). Renderers built around one engine do
not transfer. StreamRender-H3 and Streaming CWM learned a single
representation from a racing game and from CARLA, and rate 580 and 1075
overall on the generalization benchmark against 1441 for ours.
Cosmos-Transfer2.5 and Wan2.2-VACE-Fun trace the edges of the structure
closely, yet their appearance falls so far behind that they rate below
400. The strongest competitor, LynnReal-Omni, ties with ours in overall
preference on the generalization benchmark (1441 each) and trails by 100
points on the in-distribution test set, while its structure rating is
about 95 points lower on both. LynnReal-Omni labels the type of each reference, whereas our method reads untyped,
frame-aligned structure, which tightens its control .
Its total automatic score also exceeds every external renderer on both sets,
with balanced quality and structural agreement.

Causal Streaming. The causal variant of our method renders each block from past frames only
and outputs it as soon as it is sampled. It rates 1191 and 1199 overall on
the two test sets, below the bidirectional model at 1441 and 1510 but well
above the streaming renderers, Streaming CWM at 1075 and 988 and
StreamRender-H3 at 580 and 651 ( \cref tab:main). Its structure rating
stays close to ours and on the in-distribution test set even exceeds our
Stage 1 model (1313 against 1308), so that causal attention mainly costs
appearance, as later blocks drift from the colours of the first frame,
while the learned control carries over to block-by-block
generation.

外观,随着后期块从第一帧的颜色漂移,

生成。

Generalization to Unseen Representations. \Cref fig:by-repr groups the representations into categories. Ours is
ahead of LongLive-Plug on every category, seen or unseen, from block-outs
and semantic maps to pose skeletons, drawings, image buffers, and 3D
primitives, by + 0.25 +0.25 to + 0.69 +0.69 . Against our own 50-step model, the
four-step model is preferred on body and pose ( + 0.45 +0.45 ) and drawings
( + 0.41 +0.41 ), so acceleration costs little on unseen structure. Since no
reference carries a type identifier, the control LoRA cannot specialize
to a format and instead learns to read layout and motion from whatever
occupies the position of a target frame. A single control LoRA therefore generalizes to unseen structure .

blocks.en:
Comparison with the Backbone. Without the control LoRA, the official backbone treats the structural
video as a generic reference and rarely follows its layout. Its structure
rating is 627 on the generalization benchmark and 554 on the
in-distribution test set, against 1338 and 1386 for ours
( \cref tab:main), so the control comes entirely from a lightweight LoRA
on top of a frozen backbone. Our 50-step Stage 1 model already follows the
structure, which shows that the native reference pathway with a single
control LoRA suffices for control, but it renders blurrier frames. The
four-step final model rates higher on both test sets, 1441 against 1389
and 1510 against 1299 overall, and renders 12.3 times faster.

结构,它显示一个单一的本地参考路径

两个测试组的四步最后模型率较高,为1441比1389
以及1510比1299,使速度加快12.3倍。

five renderers, using the structural inputs from their demonstration cases. Ours produces sharper furniture boundaries in
SceneCraft [ Yang et al., 2024 ] and clearer character silhouettes
in the neon scene from Programmable World Model. In the Magpie scene, the bridge railings follow the
block-out more closely, while the CWM example preserves the roadside layout
and resolves the water tower. The Cosmos example preserves the tabletop layout from edge input.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We presented \texorpdfstring \pdfxform D SolarRenderer, a few-step generative renderer that turns structure
from game engines and coding agents into realistic video. Structural videos
enter the native reference pathway of a frozen MiniMax-H3 backbone without
any type identifier, so that a single control LoRA follows arbitrary
structural representations, and structure-guided distribution matching
adapts a pretrained four-step LoRA to this control model. Trained on 136K
frame-aligned clips from game engines, simulators, and YouTube videos, our method achieves state-of-the-art results on both the in-distribution test
set and the generalization benchmark, and generalizes to representations
never seen in training, while rendering 12.3 times faster than 50-step sampling. Its block-causal
variant further renders 768p video in real time .

blocks.en: A.1 Implementation Details

blocks.en:
The backbone is the official MiniMax-H3 33B Ref2VA model and stays frozen
throughout. The control LoRA has rank 384 on the attention and
feed-forward layers and is trained with the native flow-matching
objective of the backbone on clips of 158 frames at 1344 × 768 1344\times 768 and
24 fps, using AdamW [ Loshchilov and Hutter, 2019 ] with a learning rate of 10 − 4 10^{-4} for 38,400 steps at a batch of 4.
For structure-guided post-training, the control LoRA is frozen and the
teacher is the backbone with the control LoRA. The four-step LoRA has rank
384, with its first 128 ranks initialized from the pretrained DMAD LoRA
and the rest at zero, and the fake-score model is a separate LoRA
initialized at the teacher. The generator is updated once every five
fake-score updates, with learning rates of 10 − 5 10^{-5} for the generator and 2 × 10 − 6 2\times 10^{-6} for the fake-score model, for 800 iterations at a batch of 4 with w = 1.5 w=1.5 . The conditioning and data ablations use an earlier data mixture.
The causal control LoRA ( \cref sec:causal) starts from the control LoRA
after 38,400 steps and is trained with teacher forcing for 19,200 steps at a
batch of 2, using AdamW with a learning rate of 3 × 10 − 5 3\times 10^{-5} . The
causal acceleration LoRA starts from the bidirectional four-step LoRA and
is trained for 1,600 iterations at a batch of 1 with the causal control LoRA
frozen. The generator and the fake-score model, a rank-128 LoRA initialized
at the teacher, use learning rates of 2 × 10 − 5 2\times 10^{-5} and 5 × 10 − 5 5\times 10^{-5} , with five fake-score updates per generator update.
All schedules are given for one 8-GPU node, as in the released
configurations; the released weights were trained on as many
samples at a larger batch.

target frames and preserving the spatial detail of the structural input.

Training Data. The lower block of \cref tab:injection-full compares data variants.
Keeping only structured samples raises control but lowers stability and
first-frame preservation, leaving the automatic total unchanged at the
reported precision. Removing misaligned structural supervision improves
quality, stability, and control over using all data, raising the total
from 66.2 to 66.5. The corpus therefore benefits from combining reliable
structural supervision with appearance-only samples. Reducing the data
to one tenth has a smaller effect than the variation between full-data
runs, consistent with prioritizing alignment over data volume.
